D_rex_fleet_cover_standard.text: COVER PRODUCTION STANDARD: This is a finished full-color portrait comic cover, not an interior story page. Sell one dominant issue-specific idea in one glance. Maintain prestige political-space-opera realism, lived-in human stakes, clean focal hierarchy, and strong thumbnail readability. Prefer iconic issue-specific staging over recap collage. Do not default to generic cast lineups, floating-head montage, fake action, unscripted spectacle, or visual clutter. Preserve a clean trade-dress zone. The image must remain compelling before the reader knows the plot and must not reveal later issue solutions, reversals, winners, deaths, signatures, or outcomes beyond the recipe's explicit spoiler ceiling.

D_rex_fleet_cover_trade_dress.text: COVER TRADE-DRESS REFERENCE GATE: Before generating any Rex Fleet cover, retrieve and visually pixel-read the exact approved Issue 1 cover asset at production/references/rex-fleet/assets/covers/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.jpg. It is an exact byte-for-byte copy of the released StarSplitterVisions Green Corridor cover. Use that image as authority for the Rex Fleet masthead, Star Splitter Visions mark, cream/gold title typography, title scale, top-left logo placement, top-right ISSUE # block, gold divider/tagline treatment, border/line rhythm, and bottom emblem system. Use it for cover branding only. Do NOT copy Issue 1's character montage, faction split, pose, camera angle, background composition, or issue-specific art into later covers unless the current cover recipe independently requires it. The current issue recipe controls the selling image.

D_rex_fleet_cover_commercial_read.text: COMMERCIAL COVER READ TEST: Design for three reads. ONE-SECOND READ: one dominant silhouette/relationship must communicate the issue hook at phone-thumbnail size. THREE-SECOND READ: the reader should discover the contradiction or decision pressure that makes the image irresistible. TEN-SECOND READ: secondary worldbuilding, faction language, props and environmental detail may reward inspection without changing the first read. Preserve the canonical Issue 1 trade-dress footprint: keep critical faces, decisive props and the main story silhouette out of the masthead/tagline and bottom-emblem zones. If detail competes with the issue hook, remove detail. A beautiful cover that reads as generic space opera, generic action, generic ensemble poster or generic cyberpunk has failed.
